title: Inkwell
about: Rubber hose cartoons, after Fleischer's Out of the Inkwell, arranged down a tunnel. The pen is thin and hard: bold comes from contrast -- near-black ink against fills at full saturation on a dark card -- not from thickness. Arms, stems, spouts and handles are hoses that bend in a curve instead of hinging at a joint. The shapes are used as masks: each is filled with a log-polar tunnel of its own, drawn in the subject's local coordinates so the pattern travels and squashes with the shape, and with the faces off (the default) the interiors are what carry the picture. The layout is the same trick one level up -- log(r) against the angle, repeated on both -- so the cast recedes forever, with Spin and Zoom one term each, in cycles per beat. Faces and props are decided per cell rather than globally: sliders set how strong they are and how many of the cast have one, so a row of five can be two with eyes, one of those with a mouth, and a couple carrying something. Faces are off by default and C Change can bring them in across a build. Every prop is a piece of business -- steam off the teapot, a leaf off the tree, a bee round the flower, a hat that will not stay on. Colour is a small palette, quantised, rather than a continuous rainbow, which is what stops work like this looking like a screensaver, and the interior pattern chooses between guilloche, halftone, op rings and the spiral. Sixteen subjects -- face, bird, tree, lamp, trolley, teapot, flower, fish, umbrella, toadstool, cactus, snail, ice cream, alarm clock, rocket, balloon -- and they dance: a hop, a squash on the landing, a rock from the feet and a shimmy across, each one a step behind the last. Reactivity is the standard three slots, see docs/reactive.md.
